samples.question: The picture contains exactly two dark cords in two far-apart parts of the image, and the two cords never touch each other. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness with two free ends. On each cord one end is covered by a black square, which marks that cord's start; the other end is bare. One cord (the pace cord) carries exactly one gray disk sitting on it. The other cord (the roster cord) carries exactly three disks of distinct colours (red, green, blue) sitting on it. For a disk, its depth is the distance travelled along its own cord from that cord's black start square to the disk, divided by that cord's whole length from its black start square to its bare end. Depth is therefore a fraction between 0 and 1, and the two cords may have very different total lengths. Which coloured disk on the roster cord has a depth closest to the gray disk's depth on the pace cord? Answer red, green, or blue.
